_comment: Two lists of tool names, each matched on the name after its last '__' (light__HassLightSet -> HassLightSet). actions: a call to one of these changes something in the home and needs a command in what the user said (guard.py); for the guard, a tool not listed passes. reads: tools that only look something up. For the claim check (claims.py), a successful result from any tool not in reads backs a confirmation, so a tool that acts but is missing from actions (HassBroadcast, the other timer tools, an intent_script) still counts, and claims.scope_tools would give a re-run for later or for a lookup only the tools in reads, but the proxy makes only the "act" re-run today (all tools); a claim in a request for later gets CLAIM_REPLY with no re-run. A tool can be in both: search_media needs a command but only searches, so it backs no claim. A new read tool belongs in reads, or a claim after it is spoken unchecked.
_comment_particles: on/off/up/down count as a command only when the request is not a question ('kitchen lights off' yes, 'is the light on' no).
_comment_nouns: Like particles, these and any number make a request a command when it is not a question: 'volume 30', 'ten minute timer', 'thermostat to 72'.
_comment_claims: claims.py: a text reply to a command that matches one of claim_phrases (regular expressions on the lowercased reply) needs a result in the same turn, from a tool not in reads, that was not an error. A reply that ends in '?' asks back and is never checked. Otherwise the proxy re-asks once with rerun_note added to the user's message: a tool call from the re-run goes to Home Assistant, a reply that claims nothing is spoken, and another claim, an empty reply or a failed re-run gets CLAIM_REPLY, as does a claim streamed before the upstream connection failed. later_phrases mark a request for later: it gets no re-run, so no tool that acts now is offered for it.
rerun_note: Use a tool to do this. Never say it is done unless the tool ran.
